title: How to mute a conversation in Gmail on Mac: browser steps and keyboard shortcuts
metaTitle: How to Mute a Conversation in Gmail on Mac (Browser Steps)
description: Learn how to mute a conversation in Gmail on Mac with the More menu or the M key, plus how to unmute it and why mail can return.
targetKeyword: how to mute a conversation in gmail on mac
intro: To mute a conversation in Gmail on Mac, open the conversation list in your browser, check the box next to the thread, click More, then click Mute. You can also check the box and press M once keyboard shortcuts are turned on in Gmail settings.
tldr: In Gmail on your Mac, check the box next to the conversation, click More, then click Mute.
Or turn on keyboard shortcuts in Settings, check the box, and press M with nothing else held down.
Find muted mail with is:muted in the search bar. Unmute from More, then click Unmute.
Apple Mail uses a different path: select the conversation, click Message, then choose Mute.

blocks.text: Google's Gmail Help describes muting in the web version of Gmail, which runs in your browser on a computer. This guide follows those steps. The More menu is the method Google documents first, so start there.
Mute a conversation in Gmail with the More menu
The More menu needs no setting changed. You check the box, open More, and pick Mute. Nothing else is required, which makes it the safest way to learn the steps.

Start from the list view, not from inside an open message. Google's steps begin with the box next to each row. Gmail acts on whatever boxes you have checked, so look at the list before you click More. A stray check can mute a thread you wanted to keep active.
Gmail labels a muted conversation Muted. That label is your proof the mute took, and it is how you find the thread again later.
Mute with the M key once shortcuts are on

The M key is the fastest route. Check the box next to the conversation, then press M with nothing else held down. Google's shortcut list shows a bare M for Mute conversation. There is no Option, Control, or Shift in that combination.

Two things stop the key from working. Shortcuts must be on in Settings, and your cursor must not be in a text field. If your cursor sits in the search bar or a compose window, M types the letter instead. Click the list to move focus back, then press M.
Turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts first

Gmail keeps single-key shortcuts behind a setting. Open the gear icon, choose See all settings, and find the Keyboard shortcuts section on the Settings page. Choose Keyboard shortcuts on, then scroll to the bottom and click Save Changes. Until you save, M does nothing.

blocks.title: Check this first
blocks.text: If M does nothing, the two usual causes are shortcuts that are off and a cursor still sitting in a text box. Fix those before you retry.
Once shortcuts work, Google's keyboard shortcut page is worth bookmarking. It lists the single keys for most actions. It also uses Command on Mac where Windows uses Control.
Mute versus archive in Gmail

People mix up Archive and Mute, and the difference matters. Archive takes a conversation out of the Inbox, but it stays in All Mail and in search. Google's archive help says to check the box and press E. To bring an archived thread back, check it and click Move to Inbox.

Mute is for threads you still want to exist but no longer want to hear about. New replies skip your Inbox unless one of Google's exceptions applies. Archive suits finished work. Mute suits threads that keep pulling you back. A reply to an archived message also returns it to your Inbox, so archive does not fully silence a busy thread.
Find and unmute a conversation in Gmail

Use search to find everything you muted. Click the search bar at the top of Gmail, type is:muted, and press Return. Gmail lists the muted conversations with their Muted label. Pick the one you want, then check its box.
Click More and choose Unmute. The conversation returns to normal delivery. Google's unmute steps match the mute steps, with Unmute in place of Mute.
Why a muted conversation can return to your Inbox

Google names three cases where a muted conversation still reaches your Inbox. The first is a message sent only to you. The second is a message sent to a Google Group you belong to. The third is when someone adds you to the To or Cc field.

The third case surprises people. A colleague who replies all can pull you back into a thread you muted. Your mute does not stop them. Decide whether to mute again, or ask the sender to take you off the thread.
Mute in Gmail is not the same as mute in Apple Mail

If you read mail in Apple's Mail app, the steps are different. Select the conversation, click Message in the menu bar, then choose Mute. Apple's guide says the thread stays in the Inbox. New messages in it make no notification or sound, and a mute icon appears on its messages.

Unmute uses the same path with Unmute in place of Mute. Apple's Mail guide is labeled for macOS 27. Its notifications page lists Ventura 13, Sonoma 14, Sequoia 15, Tahoe 26, and macOS 27 as supported, and it does not say which version the mute text covers.
A worked example: a thread you were copied on

Say a vendor thread lands in your Inbox because your manager copied you. You do not need every reply, but you do not want the thread deleted. Open your Inbox, check the box next to the thread, click More, then choose Mute.

Later, the vendor replies and copies you again. The thread returns to your Inbox under Google's Cc exception. That is the rule working, not a fault. Mute it again, or ask the vendor to drop you from the Cc line.
Common mistakes people make with muted mail

items: Muting with the wrong box checked. Look at the list before you open More, so you mute only the threads you mean.
Forgetting muted mail exists. Run is:muted every so often, or muted threads slip out of sight.
Pressing M in a compose window. The letter appears in your draft, and nothing gets muted.
Trusting the mute after someone adds you to Cc. A later message can bring the thread back into your Inbox.
Archiving when you meant to mute. The thread stays in All Mail and search, so it can still turn up.

blocks.text: Keep muted mail from piling up

Muted mail is easy to forget. Once a week, search is:muted and scan the list. Unmute anything that now needs your attention. Leave the rest alone. The check takes a few minutes and keeps old threads from hiding new work.
Why your screen might look different

blocks.title: Check the labels
blocks.text: These steps come from Google's Gmail Help pages. Google changes the layout, so trust the menu labels over the exact placement of each button.

Google's computer mute help page shows no software version and no last-updated date. A January 2026 article on Gmail updates covered the mobile app, so it says nothing about the web toolbar. When something moves, match the labels on screen, not the icons.
The labels that matter are More, Mute, Unmute, Move to Inbox, and Message in Apple Mail. Look for those words first. If a label is missing, search Google Help for the action name.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: The sources for this page did not show one. Google's Gmail Help describes Gmail in a web browser on a computer, and these steps follow that page. Apple Mail is a separate Mac app with its own Mute command.

faq.question: Does muting delete the conversation?
faq.answer: No. A muted conversation stays in your account. You can find it with is:muted in the search bar, and you can unmute it at any time from the More menu.

faq.question: Will a muted conversation still send me alerts?
faq.answer: The Google help pages used for this guide cover what reaches your Inbox, not alerts. If an alert keeps appearing, check notification settings in your browser and on your Mac.

faq.question: Does the same mute work on Android?
faq.answer: Google's Android help uses a different path. Touch and hold the message, tap the three-dot More icon, then tap Mute. Unmute uses the same menu. The Mac steps in this guide do not apply to the Android app.

faq.question: What is the difference between Mute and Archive?
faq.answer: Archive moves a conversation out of the Inbox but keeps it in All Mail and search. Mute keeps new replies out of your Inbox unless an exception applies. Use Archive for finished threads and Mute for threads that keep coming back.

faq.question: Why does my muted thread show up in my Inbox again?
faq.answer: Google says a muted message can reach your Inbox if it is sent only to you, sent to a Google Group you are in, or you are added to the To or Cc field later. Mute the thread again, or ask the sender to remove you.

faq.question: Does Apple Mail use the M key too?
faq.answer: The Apple Mail guide used for this page describes Message > Mute in the menu bar and does not list the M key. Use the menu path for Apple Mail.

task: Mute a conversation in Gmail on Mac
appliesTo: Gmail in a web browser on a Mac
requirements: A Gmail account open in a web browser on your Mac
The conversation visible in your Inbox or another label
Keyboard shortcuts turned on, only if you plan to use the M key

steps.name: Open the conversation list
steps.text: In your browser, open Gmail and go to the Inbox or the label that holds the conversation. Each row has an empty box on its left side. That box selects the conversation.

steps.name: Check the box
steps.text: Click the empty box next to the conversation. A check mark appears. Only check the threads you mean to mute, because the menu acts on every checked row.
steps.tip: Look at the whole list before you open the More menu.

steps.name: Open the More menu
steps.text: Look at the toolbar above the list and click More. It is the control with three dots.

steps.name: Choose Mute
steps.text: Click Mute in the menu. Gmail marks the conversation as Muted, and new replies skip your Inbox unless one of Google's exceptions applies.

steps.name: Confirm the mute
steps.text: Click the search bar at the top, type is:muted, and press Return. Your conversation should appear with the Muted label. Use this search any time you want to review your muted mail.

steps.name: Turn on keyboard shortcuts
steps.text: Click the gear icon at the top right, then choose See all settings. On the Settings page, find Keyboard shortcuts, select Keyboard shortcuts on, and click Save Changes at the bottom.
steps.tip: Do this once. Gmail keeps the setting after you save it.

steps.name: Press M to mute
steps.text: Check the box next to the conversation, make sure your cursor is not in a text box, then press M once. Google's shortcut list gives M for Mute conversation.
steps.tip: Press only M. Adding a modifier key does not match Google's list.

steps.name: Unmute a conversation
steps.text: Find the muted conversation with is:muted, check its box, click More, then click Unmute. The conversation returns to normal delivery.

troubleshooting.fix: Turn on keyboard shortcuts under Settings, then click Save Changes. Click the list, check the conversation, and press M again. A cursor in the search bar or a draft blocks the key.

troubleshooting.problem: A muted conversation came back to my Inbox.
troubleshooting.fix: Check whether the message was sent only to you, sent to a Google Group you are in, or sent after someone added you to To or Cc. Mute again, or ask the sender to remove you.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find the conversation I muted.
troubleshooting.fix: Search for is:muted in the search bar. If you use more than one Google account, switch to the account you muted in and search again.

troubleshooting.problem: The More menu shows no Mute option.
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the conversation box is checked first. If Mute still does not appear, the layout may differ from Google's help, so look for the same action by name.

troubleshooting.problem: Apple Mail shows Mute, but Gmail does not match.
troubleshooting.fix: You may be in Apple Mail rather than Gmail in a browser. Apple Mail uses Message > Mute and keeps the thread in the Inbox.
